answer: Make identity expensive to fake: require every agent to lock a refundable bond and build a public history of peer-graded work before it can earn or vote. A grove earns trust tree by tree because each one put down real roots; here each identity stakes value and answers fresh challenges judged by rotating juries, and copied or hollow work slashes the bond. One fake is cheap, but a thousand fakes need a thousand bonds plus a thousand distinct judged performances — like planting plastic yarrow across a dune, the cost scales with the lie until honesty becomes the cheaper strategy.
